cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still speaking to all Israel east of the Jordan, in the land of Moab (Deuteronomy 1:1, 5). Now he turns to looking out for your brother's things. If you see your brother's ox or sheep straying, Moses says you must not ignore it.

cards.question: You spot your brother's ox or sheep straying. What does Moses say to do?

answers.text: Bring it to the city elders

cards.text: Easy when your brother lives right down the road. But what if he lives FAR away, or you have NO idea whose ox is standing in front of you?

cards.question: What if your brother lives far away, or you don't know whose stray animal it is? What does Moses say to do?

answers.text: Take it home until he comes for it
Sell it and save the money for him
Turn it loose back into the field

cards.text: Moses says this goes for more than your brother's ox or sheep. I spent YEARS lost in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so I am ALL in on this law.

cards.question: Moses says the same goes for your brother's donkey, his cloak, or anything your brother has lost and you have found.
Moses says that if your brother's donkey or ox has fallen on the road, you should wait until it gets up on its own.

cards.text: Then a rule about clothes. A woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing.

cards.question: Moses says a woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing. How does he say the LORD your God sees whoever does these things?

cards.text: Next, a bird's nest along the road, in a tree or on the ground, with the mother sitting on the chicks or eggs. You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go.

cards.question: Moses attaches a promise to letting the mother bird go. What is it?

answers.text: That you may prolong your days
That your harvest may be great

cards.text: A long-life promise, over a BIRD'S NEST. Next up, Moses the BUILDING INSPECTOR: if you build a new house, put a railing around your roof.

cards.question: Moses says a roof railing keeps you from bringing ___ on your house if someone falls from it.

cards.text: Then Moses gives some no-mixing rules for your vineyard, your plowing and your clothes. Do not plant your vineyard with two types of seed, he says, or the entire harvest will be defiled. He wraps up with tassels on the four corners of your cloak.
Now Moses turns to marriage, and things get serious. Suppose a man marries, comes to hate his wife, and accuses her of shameful conduct, saying she was not a virgin.

cards.question: A husband has given his wife a bad name. Who brings the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate?

cards.text: Her parents stand before the elders at the gate. They say, "I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he has come to hate her."

cards.question: Her parents spread out the cloth before the elders, and it shows the husband's accusation is false. What do the elders do to him?

answers.text: Send him out of the city

cards.question: After his false accusation, the husband is still allowed to divorce his wife.

cards.text: She remains his wife, and he must not divorce her as long as he lives. But if the accusation is true and no proof can be found, it goes the other way, and she is to be stoned to death.
Moses calls it an outrage in Israel and says, "So you must purge the evil from among you." Then he takes up a man found lying with another man's wife.

cards.question: A man is found lying with another man's wife. Moses says only the woman must die.

cards.text: Next, a virgin pledged in marriage to a man. Another man encounters her in the city and sleeps with her.

cards.question: A man sleeps with a virgin pledged in marriage, in the city, and both of them are stoned at the gate. What reason does Moses give for the young woman?

answers.text: She did not cry out in the city
She did not tell her family
She lied to the city elders

cards.text: And the man is stoned because he has violated his neighbor's wife. But now Moses changes the place to the open country, where a man overpowers a betrothed woman and lies with her.

cards.question: In the open country, only the man who overpowers the betrothed woman must die.

cards.text: Moses says, "Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death." She cried out in that field, but there was no one to save her.

cards.question: Moses says the case of a man who overpowers a betrothed woman in the open country is just like one in which a man attacks his ___ and murders him.

cards.text: Next case: a man seizes a virgin who isn't pledged in marriage, lies with her, and they are discovered. He must pay her father fifty shekels of silver.

cards.question: The man pays the young woman's father fifty shekels of silver. What else does the law require of him?

answers.text: He must marry her and never divorce her
He must leave the city and never return
He must serve her father for seven years

cards.question: Moses ends with a law about a man's own family. Who is a man not to marry?

cards.text: And Moses is still going, friend. His speech isn't over yet.
